- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and then gradually correct — but often overcorrects, leading to prolonged overestimation.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting a mean-reversion bias or lag in capturing downward momentum.
- Forecasts show higher variance than actuals, particularly in the middle of the horizon, indicating overconfidence in short-term volatility.
- Model fails to capture sharp downward corrections after prolonged upward trends — often misses the “bottom” of a correction.
- When true prices show a clear downward trend, model continues to project upward or flat, suggesting lag in trend reversal detection.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — underestimates sharp drops and overestimates gradual declines.
- Forecasts are often too optimistic in the first 10 days, then too pessimistic in the last 10 days — suggesting asymmetric bias toward early overestimation and late underestimation.
